appraisal_events.evidence: "ajouta-t-elle, en dévoilant dans un sourire une satisfaction de vanité qu'elle ne s'apercevait plus ne pas pouvoir paraître légitime à Swann"; ends with her fishing for approval: "Elle a du bon, tout de même, tu vois, ta petite Odette, quoiqu'on la trouve si détestable."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator notes that Odette takes vain satisfaction in being pursued by a procuress and an ambassador, oblivious that such pride cannot read as legitimate to a jealous Swann, subtly undercutting her self-presentation in this anecdote.

status_effects.explanation: Her vain, tone-deaf pride in her own anecdote (about being pursued by disreputable go-betweens) is mildly undercut by the narrator, distinct from Swann's already-scored suffering.

ambiguities: The passage also frames Odette as only 'half guilty' given a hard childhood ('livrée, presque enfant, à Nice, à un riche Anglais'), which softens blame on her; this was treated as instrumental to depicting Swann's own psychological coping (already captured by the accepted annotation's focus on his suffering) rather than a distinct local status movement for Odette, and so was not separately scored.

M. Verdurin appears only as part of the collective 'les Verdurin' marking a painful season/location for Swann's memory, with no distinct evaluative content of his own, so he was omitted as a candidate.
Neither le narrateur nor duchesse de Guermantes appears in this passage, which is entirely third-person narration centered on Swann and Odette; both were omitted.
